text:
Michelle (Design): Quick check — trying to settle on copy and UX for the alerts preview + snooze/mute affordance. Posting a short mock and a11y questions. pls weigh in 🙏 Samir (FE): Nice, can you paste the mock link? Michelle (Design): https://mock.redwood.ai/s/alerts/snooze-v2.png — the key bits: action pills show "Snooze" vs "Mute" vs "Suppress", and a tiny preview panel that reads out which channels will fire. Dan (PM): TL;DR: users confuse snooze and suppress. Snooze = temporary; suppress = block notifications for a group. We should make duration explicit next to Snooze. Leah (UX Research): Data from our last study — 60% used "snooze" expecting a mute for a single alert not a group. Wording alone didn't fix it. Maybe combine icon + short helper text. Aria (A11y): A11y notes: when you toggle a suppression the preview panel updates; we need an aria-live region to announce "Notifications suppressed for 2h for channel: Slack, Email" so screen readers see the change. Also keyboard focus after the action should remain on the changed control. Samir (FE): FWIW implementation approach: we can keep pills and add a small inline chevron for duration picker. Quick snippet for aria-live I was thinking: ```
Notifications will be sent to: Slack, Email
``` But Aria — is polite ok or do we need assertive for immediate suppression? Aria (A11y): Use polite for non-critical updates. If suppression means preventing incidents, that's still informational. Keep polite unless it's blocking user flow. Also ensure role="status" fallback for older AT. Michelle (Design): Copy options I'm weighing: - Option A: "Snooze for 2 hours" (hover: pauses notifications for this incident) - Option B: "Mute for 2 hours" (hover: pause notifications from this rule) - Option C: "Suppress (group) — 2h" (hover: suppresses alerts for selected channels) Dan (PM): I prefer "Snooze — 2h" for single-alert, "Suppress — 2h (group)" for multi-alert groups. Avoid "Mute"; too ambiguous with OS mute. Leah (UX Research): Microcopy suggestion: add a one-line helper under the pill when expanded: "Snooze pauses notifications for this alert instance. Suppress blocks notifications for the entire rule and selected channels." Small, plain language. Samir (FE): Visual nit: when preview updates, we animate height. Need to avoid focus loss. I'll drop a tiny CSS plan: max-height anim + prefers-reduced-motion check. Michelle (Design): Accessibility flow question: after user selects "Suppress for 2h" we show a toast and the preview says "Suppressed: Slack, Email". Do we also focus the toast? Thoughts? Aria (A11y): Don't move focus to toast unless it's actionable. Announce via aria-live and leave focus where it is. If toast has a "Undo" action we should make that keyboard reachable (tabindex=0) and focusable. Dan (PM): Product constraint — Undo must be present for 30s. Suggest we show inline "Undo" button next to pill (aria-label="Undo suppress"). Michelle (Design): UX question — preview order: should it be channel-priority (PagerDuty > Slack > Email) or frequency (most-likely > fallback)? The mock shows priority. Leah (UX Research): Participants expect primary channel first. Keep priority, but show a "primary" badge on the channel chip for clarity. Samir (FE): Implementation detail: channel chips have a drag handle in another view. For preview we should avoid drag affordances — purely read-only chips with badge. noti-bot: Preview updated: Primary channels: PagerDuty, Slack — Secondary: Email. Michelle (Design): Small copy nits: change "Notifications will be sent to" -> "These channels will notify you" (shorter). Does that read ok? Dan (PM): Shorter is good. Make sure we include a tooltip for full rule name on hover. Aria (A11y): Tooltip must be aria-describedby and keyboard accessible (focusable). Use role="tooltip" and ensure it appears on focus, not only hover. Leah (UX Research): Quick A/B idea: show helper text under pill vs a tiny info icon which opens a modal. We should test which reduces mis-clicks. Michelle (Design): Vote: - A: Inline helper under pill (1 sentence) — @Leah, @Samir - B: Info icon -> modal with details — @Dan, @Aria Samir (FE): 👍 for A (less context switching). Leah (UX Research): 👍 A. Dan (PM): 🤔 leaning B for discoverability. Aria (A11y): A is cleaner for keyboard users. Modal adds complexity for screen readers unless properly labelled. Michelle (Design): OK — leaning A. I'll update the mock to show a 1-line helper and explicit primary badges. Punting modal test to later. Dan (PM): Also can we add a short tooltip on the pill that shows "Undo available for 30s" after action? Samir (FE): Yep — simple aria-live update + an Undo button with aria-label will do. Michelle (Design): Great. Action items: - Michelle: update mock (add helper text + primary badge) and copy variants (today) - Samir: add aria-live snippet + reduced-motion CSS note (tomorrow) - Aria: draft a short a11y checklist for the flow (focus, live region, undo keyboard) (EOD) - Leah: schedule 5-min moderated test for the two copy variants (this week) Dan (PM): I'll coordinate rollout and hook up analytics event for "snooze vs suppress" clicks. Michelle (Design): Thanks all — will drop updated image and short diff when ready. ✨
